{{Quote|Ah. Red Six. Tough call sign. We lost a Red Six at the first Death Star battle, too. Jek Porkins, and R5-D8.|translated=1|R2-D2, to BB-8|<ref name="PD28">[[Poe Dameron 28|''Poe Dameron'' 28]]</ref>}}
'''R5-D8''' was an [[R5 series astromech droid]] manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]] that served in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]'s [[Massassi Group]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. During the [[Battle of Yavin]], it flew with [[Rebel pilot]] [[Jek Tono Porkins|Jek Porkins]] as [[Red Six]]. R5-D8 was destroyed during the battle when Porkins' [[Red Six (T-65B X-wing starfighter)|X-wing]] [[starfighter]] was blown to pieces by enemy fire.

==Biography==
R5-D8<ref name="LEGO">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''</ref> was the designation of an [[R5 series astromech droid|R5 unit]] that served in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the [[Galactic Civil War]] against the [[Galactic Empire]]. It was part of the rebel<ref name="Episode IV" /> [[Massassi Group]]<ref name="Massassi Group">The episode "[[Zero Hour]]" states that the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] forces stationed on [[Yavin 4]] are known as the [[Massassi Group]]. As [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] shows R5-D8 to be part of [[Red Squadron]], which is based on Yavin IV, the [[droid]] must be part of the Massassi Group.</ref> based in the [[Great Temple]] on the [[moon]] [[Yavin 4]] and flew in a [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]] with [[Rebel pilot]] [[Jek Tono Porkins|Jek Porkins]] as [[Red Six]] in [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]].<ref name="Episode IV" />

During the [[Battle of Yavin]], the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[superweapon]] entered the [[Yavin system]] with the aim of destroying Yavin 4 and the rebels based there. R5-D8 and the rest of [[Color|Red]] [[Squadron]] were part of the force mobilized to try and destroy the [[Death Star]]. During the battle they engaged the [[turbolaser]] [[turret]]s on the superweapon's surface in order to draw fire from the [[BTL-A4 Y-wing assault starfighter/bomber|BTL-A4 Y-wing starfighters]] of [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]].<ref name="Episode IV" />

[[File:Roasted_Porkins.png|thumb|left|250px|R5-D8 perished during the Battle of Yavin.]]
After R5-D8 and Porkins provided cover for fellow rebel [[Biggs Darklighter]] as he destroyed a [[Deflection tower/Canon|deflection tower]] on the Death Star's surface,<ref name="Episode IV" /> the pair's [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing]] developed a mechanical fault that left Porkins struggling to maneuver. Before R5-D8 or Porkins could fix the problem,<ref name="Databank">{{Databank|jek-porkins|Jek Porkins}}</ref> they both perished when their X-wing starfighter was destroyed by enemy fire. The rebels ultimately destroyed the Death Star and won the battle.<ref name="Episode IV" /> Around [[34 ABY|thirty four years later]],<ref name="Date2">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens|''Star Wars'': Episode VII ''The Force Awakens'']] to [[34 ABY]]. [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']] takes place immediately after the events of ''The Force Awakens'', and [[Poe Dameron 28|''Poe Dameron'' 28]] takes place immediately after that, so the events of ''Poe Dameron 28'' must also take place in approximately 34 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]].</ref> the astromech [[R2-D2]], who had flown with [[Luke Skywalker]] as [[Red Five]] at [[Yavin Prime|Yavin]], remembered R5-D8's sacrifice and told the [[Resistance]] astromech [[BB-8]] about the [[droid]].<ref name="PD28" />

==Description==
R5-D8 was an [[R-series|R5 unit]] [[astromech droid]] with [[Color|white]] plating detailed with red.<ref name="Episode IV" /> Like all R5 units, it was manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton]] and stood ninety-seven [[Meter|centimeters]] tall.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:R5-D8_Lego.png|thumb|right|R5-D8 in LEGO form|200px]]
R5-D8 first appeared as a prop in the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']].<ref name="Episode IV" /> The character's name was first confirmed to be [[canon]] in the [[2015]] video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''.<ref name="LEGO">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''</ref> Despite the game being non-canon, [[Pablo Hidalgo]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] confirmed that the names provided by the game, which included R5-D8, were considered canon.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|pablohidalgo|status/749616406245699584|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2016-07-03|quote=@LelalMekha Yeah, same with Infinity.|archivefile=File:PabloHidalgo-LegoName-Twitter.png|nolive=1}} {{C|In response to: "@pablohidalgo <nowiki>youtube.com/watch?v=JwxAeHPLpPg</nowiki> The Lego game identifies a few BG characters from TFA, but are those names canonical?"}} — [[Pablo Hidalgo]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]] confirmed that the character names introduced in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]'' are considered [[canon]], despite the [[Star Wars video games|video game]] itself being non-canon.</ref>

The name originated in [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]], where it was first used in [[2000]] in a "Force File" included with a Jek Porkins action figure released by [[Hasbro]] as part of the ''[[Star Wars: Power of the Jedi]]'' line.<ref name="Toy">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: Power of the Jedi|pack=Jek Porkins (X-Wing Pilot)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/potjporkins.asp}}</ref>
